overview: Two engineered T-cell therapy platforms that redirect a patient's own T cells against cancer, differing in how they recognize their target.
genZNote: CAR-T grabs the surface handle directly. TCR-T needs the cell to show its ID badge (MHC) first.

aspects.label: Overview / Core Definition
aspects.valueA: T cells engineered to express a chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) that directly recognizes a surface antigen on tumor cells, independent of MHC.
aspects.valueB: T cells engineered to express an affinity-enhanced T-cell receptor (TCR) that recognizes peptide antigens presented on MHC molecules.

aspects.label: Antigen Recognition
aspects.valueA: Recognizes intact surface proteins directly, MHC-independent.
aspects.valueB: Recognizes intracellular-derived peptide fragments presented on MHC, similar to natural T-cell recognition.

aspects.label: Target Antigen Scope
aspects.valueA: Limited to antigens expressed on the cell surface.
aspects.valueB: Can target both surface and intracellular proteins, since peptides from any protein can be presented on MHC.

aspects.label: MHC Restriction
aspects.valueA: Not MHC-restricted, so it works across patients with different HLA types.
aspects.valueB: MHC-restricted, meaning a given TCR-T therapy generally only works in patients with a matching HLA type.

aspects.label: Clinical Success So Far
aspects.valueA: FDA-approved for several B-cell malignancies (e.g. targeting CD19 or BCMA).
aspects.valueB: Approved and in trials mainly for solid tumors expressing specific HLA-restricted antigens (e.g. certain sarcomas, melanoma).

aspects.label: Key Distinguishing Feature
aspects.valueB: MHC-dependent recognition, can target intracellular-derived antigens.
